newsitem.title: ITALY: Milan shares end lower on ex-divs and Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Milan shares end lower on ex-divs and Wall Street.

text.p: Italian shares ended lower on Monday as many stocks went ex-dividend and investors turned cautious with Wall Street easier and as they awaited the outcome of rival offers to merge with Italy's savings bank Cariplo.

They added that some 70 companies, 13 of which are part of the MIB30 index, went ex-dividend and two of them Ambroveneto and Banca Commerciale Italiana (BCI) have made rival offers to link up with Cariplo. The Foundation that controls Cariplo is expected to announced its preferred suitor later today.
The all-share Mibtel index ended 0.58 percent lower at 12,427 while the MIB30 closed 0.74 percent down at 18,569.

Among the banking shares, BCI ended off 8.09 percent at 3,556 lire while Ambroveneto was down 4.18 percent at 4,421. San Paolo, which also went ex-div, slipped 4.08 percent to 10,660 on the first day of its public share offer.
The negative effect of the ex-div stocks was 0.88 percent on the Mibtel, dealers said. Other ex-divs were Pirelli off 2.93 percent at 3,728 and Telecom Italia down 2.18 percent at 4,622.

Among the risers, was Carlo De Benedetti's industrial holding group CIR ending up 3.97 percent at 1,074 lire after it said at the weekend that CIR intended to make a public buy offer for Sasib, in which it holds a 54.4 percent stake.
Other gainers included Fiat which ended up 1.83 percent at 5,621 lire and Montedison 2.25 percent firmer at 1,089 lire.
